extracted.intended_audience: litigation counsel, parties, eDiscovery and data-protection professionals handling cross-border discovery and protective orders
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural protections for designating, handling, securing, transferring, challenging, and disposing of Confidential/Highly Confidential and Protected Data in cross-border litigation, including a Protocol for documenting transfer safeguards. Useful for drafting protective orders and operationalizing cross-border data transfers in U.S. litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify applicable Data Protection Laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether data required to be preserved, processed, or disclosed in the U.S. is subject to Data Protection Laws and, if so, which laws apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess alternative non-protected sources of relevant data; identify specific laws (e.g., GDPR, PIPEDA, APPI, GLBA, HIPAA, national laws) and tailor/update the list to the jurisdictions implicated in the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Confidential/Highly Confidential Material
rubrics_metrics.description: The designation of Discovery Material as Confidential Material or Highly Confidential Material for purposes of this Order shall be made in the following manner: Documents; Deposition and Other Proceedings; Non-Written Materials (placeholders provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model provides section placeholders for precise procedures for documents, depositions, and non-written materials; parties should insert tailored rules for how and when designations are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertent disclosure does not waive confidentiality if remedied
rubrics_metrics.description: The inadvertent failure to designate Discovery Material as Confidential or Highly Confidential does not constitute a waiver of such claim and may be remedied by prompt supplemental written notice upon discovery of the inadvertent disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon remedy, the material becomes subject to the protections of the Order; Receiving Party must take steps (see Copies, Section 8) to ensure proper handling after notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies inherit confidentiality and must be legend-marked
rubrics_metrics.description: The Receiving Party may make copies of Discovery Material, but such copies shall become Confidential Material or Highly Confidential Material to the same extent and be subject to the same protections as the source material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Party shall exercise good faith efforts to ensure copies include the appropriate confidentiality legend; if notified of inadvertent non-designation, ensure copies are marked, access is limited to authorized persons, and they are handled per the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivatives and notes receive same confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Any notes, lists, memoranda, indices, compilations or other information that quote from, paraphrase, copy, or disclose Confidential/Highly Confidential Material with such specificity that the underlying material can be identified shall be accorded the same status of confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to electronic forms as well; these derivatives are subject to all terms of the Protective Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to non-parties subpoenaed
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party issuing a subpoena to a non-party shall enclose a copy of this Protective Order with a request that, within ten (10) calendar days, the non-party either request the protection of this Protective Order or notify the issuing party that the non-party does not need the protection or wishes to seek different protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates consistent protection for materials obtained from non-parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit who may receive Confidential Material
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery Material designated “Confidential” may be disclosed, summarized, described, characterized, or otherwise made available only to specified persons (section lists to be inserted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model includes placeholders for enumerating authorized persons; parties should specify categories (e.g., counsel, in-house counsel, experts) consistent with the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit who may receive Highly Confidential Material
rubrics_metrics.description: Highly Confidential Material shall not be disclosed to any person or entity, directly or indirectly, other than specified persons (placeholders provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must insert specific permitted recipients; protections are stricter than for 'Confidential' material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification restrictions for outside experts/consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither Confidential nor Highly Confidential Material shall be disclosed to any outside experts or consultants who are current employees of a direct competitor of any party named in the Litigation (with space for exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may add tailored exceptions; purpose is to prevent competitive harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use limitation: litigation only
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery Material containing Confidential and/or Highly Confidential Material shall be used solely for purposes of the Litigation, including any appeal and retrial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person or entity in possession of such material shall maintain those materials in accordance with the Order (e.g., storage, access controls).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signed agreement required before disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each person to whom Confidential or Highly Confidential Material may be disclosed (and who must sign Exhibit A) shall deliver a completed and originally executed copy of Exhibit A to the Disclosing Party prior to disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit A is the Agreement Concerning Information Covered By Stipulated Protective Order; it contains acknowledgments of understanding and commitment to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to exclude persons from depositions for confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Counsel for any Producing Party shall have the right to exclude from depositions any person who is not authorized by this Order to receive documents or information designated Confidential or Highly Confidential, but only during periods of examination or testimony directed to or comprising such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures confidentiality of deposition testimony that contains protected information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure storage standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients shall maintain Confidential or Highly Confidential Material in a reasonably secure and safe manner limiting access to persons authorized under the Order and exercise the same standard of care as for their own proprietary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to storage, custody, use, and dissemination; may be satisfied by vendors with appropriate information-security programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing confidential material under seal consistent with court rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for filing Confidential or Highly Confidential Material apply provided they do not conflict with applicable rules and orders of the court (presumption of public filings absent good cause for sealing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common provision: file under temporary seal with notice and a 10-day period for motions to prevent materials from becoming public; consult local rules and standing orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prejudice from agreeing to the Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreeing to be bound by this Protective Order, producing or receiving Confidential Material or otherwise complying with the Order shall not [insert rights of parties protected].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model leaves space to insert specific rights preserved; agreement to the Order is not intended to waive other legal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right and procedure to challenge confidentiality designations
rubrics_metrics.description: A party is not obligated to challenge a designation at the time made; failure to do so does not preclude a subsequent challenge during the litigation. The Order provides placeholders for steps: Challenge; Meet and Confer and Motion; Status of challenged designation pending judicial determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenged designations remain in force until the court determines their propriety; parties should insert procedural steps for challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions: public or otherwise available information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order does not limit use of information that the Receiving Party can demonstrate: (i) was lawfully in its possession prior to designation; (ii) was obtained from a third party with the right to disclose without restriction; (iii) was independently developed by personnel without access; or (iv) has been independently published to the public, and Data Protection Laws do not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Receiving Party believes information was improperly designated under these categories, it may challenge under the designation-challenge process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve privilege—no waiver by production (FRE 502(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to Federal Rule of Evidence 502(d), disclosure (including production) of information that a party later claims should not have been disclosed because of a privilege shall not constitute a waiver of any claim of attorney-client privilege, work product, or other ground for withholding production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model protects against broad waiver across proceedings when producing under the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling inadvertently produced privileged information
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to FRCP 26(b)(5)(B) and FRE 502(e), the Receiving Party agrees to return, sequester, or destroy Privileged Information upon request; if it reasonably believes such information was inadvertently produced it shall promptly notify the Producing Party and sequester the information until disposition instructions are received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide notice/instructions does not itself constitute waiver; model contains placeholder for additional steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Onboarding of additional parties/attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: If additional parties join or intervene, they shall not have access to Confidential/Highly Confidential Material until their counsel has executed and, at request, filed the agreement to be fully bound by the Order. New attorneys must execute Exhibit A before access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures continuity of protections when the litigation's participant roster changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective Order survival and court jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: This Protective Order shall remain in force until modified, superseded, or terminated by consent of the parties or by order of the Court and shall survive termination of the Litigation unless otherwise ordered; the Court retains jurisdiction after termination to enforce or amend the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may consider mediation clauses for post-termination disputes if the Court declines to retain jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prejudice to seeking further relief
rubrics_metrics.description: The Protective Order is without prejudice to any party's right to seek other or further relief from the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may pursue additional remedies as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of objections to production grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Protective Order shall not be construed as waiving any right to assert privilege, relevance, overbreadth, burdensomeness, or other grounds for not producing material called for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to disputed material remains as otherwise provided by discovery rules and applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination-of-access procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Placeholders provided for treatment on change in status and conclusion of litigation (e.g., who retains access, how access changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should insert instructions for change-in-status and end-of-litigation transitions to terminate access as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected status persists when used in court proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential/Highly Confidential Material used in court proceedings or appeals shall not lose its protected status through such use unless lawfully placed on the public record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel must comply with local rules and confer on procedures (e.g., petition to close courtroom) necessary to protect confidentiality of documents, information, and transcripts used in court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when Receiver is served with external demand
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person receiving material covered by the Order is served with a subpoena, order, or demand in another action seeking that material, the Receiver shall give prompt written notice by email within ten (10) business days to the producing party and shall object to production on the grounds of this Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden of opposing enforcement of the external Demand falls on the producing party; unless that party obtains an order directing non-compliance, the Receiver may produce on the Demand response date; compliance with another lawful subpoena does not violate the Order; ensure secure transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney-client advice allowed but limits on disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Order bars attorneys from rendering advice to their clients and referring generally to examination of Confidential/Highly Confidential Material; however, attorneys shall not disclose the contents of another party's materials if such disclosure would contravene the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances attorney-client advice with confidentiality obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction of privileged or legally protected matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Producing Party may redact matter it claims is subject to privilege, work product, legal prohibition, or other immunity; redacted pages shall be marked “REDACTED” and the basis specified; an unredacted version shall be preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model suggests inserting specifics for redaction of privileged matter from native electronic files; protected data redaction rules follow (see next entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction of Protected Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may redact Protected Data in good faith that requires protection under the Order; Protected Data shall not be redacted to the extent it directly relates to or identifies an individual named as a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protected Data shall be redacted from any public filing not filed under seal; the right and process to challenge redactions mirror the challenge process for Confidential/Highly Confidential designations (Section 20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
rubrics_metrics.description: PII designated as Protected Data based on a good faith belief it is subject to Data Protection Laws or other privacy obligations shall be handled by counsel for the Receiving Party with the highest care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes heightened handling standards for PII beyond ordinary confidentiality measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information security program requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person in possession of Confidential or Highly Confidential Material shall maintain a written information security program that includes reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect the security and confidentiality of such materials and against reasonably anticipated threats or unauthorized access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a party lacks such a program, they may comply by having the material managed/stored by eDiscovery vendors or administrators that do maintain such programs; model lists example technologies (SFTP, SSL, VPN), encryption in transit/at rest, controlled access, background checks, vendor selection, and possible liquidated-damages or contractual provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breach notification, investigation, remediation, and cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Receiving Party or Authorized Recipient discovers loss, breach, or suspected unauthorized access relating to another party’s Confidential or Highly Confidential Material, they shall: (1) promptly provide written notice to Disclosing Party; (2) investigate and make reasonable efforts to remediate and provide assurances that breach will not recur; and (3) provide sufficient information for the Disclosing Party to ascertain size and scope of the breach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiver agrees to cooperate with Producing Party and/or law enforcement and to take necessary corrective action to terminate unauthorized access.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-of-matter data disposition certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon final resolution of the Litigation the Parties will certify that all Confidential Material and/or Highly Confidential Material has been returned to the Producing Party and/or been destroyed in a secure manner (placeholders for details).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model leaves space to insert specifics about certification process and any exceptions (e.g., retained work-product copies). Parties should consider risks of destroying data subject to legal holds and may include express agreements or court orders addressing disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for violations and continued court jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of violation of the Protective Order, the aggrieved Disclosing Party may apply to the Court for relief, including injunctive relief, and the Court retains jurisdiction to enforce the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model notes injunctive relief is at the District Judge's discretion; parties agree the Court retains jurisdiction over persons subject to the Order for enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit A: recipient acknowledgement and commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient must acknowledge receipt of the Protective Order, understand its terms, agree to comply and be bound by them, agree not to further disclose or use the information except as permitted, maintain data security and end-of-matter disposition provisions, and submit to the Court's jurisdiction for resolution of matters pertaining to the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit A requires recipient contact/employer information, signature and date; Exhibit's execution is a prerequisite for access under specified sections of the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Border Protocol — explain purpose and U.S. proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the reasons for preserving or collecting the data and identify clearly the U.S. proceedings for which the Protected Data is processed and transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data is preserved/collected for reasons other than litigation, identify the legal proceeding requiring processing/transfer; include case identifiers (name, docket number, filing location).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Border Protocol — identify sources and laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the Data Protection Laws at issue and specific sources of Protected Data, assess alternative non-protected sources, and identify where data is located, processed, and transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the country and specific laws implicated and the significance of each; prefer producing non-protected sources where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Border Protocol — minimize processing and transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe measures taken to minimize the processing and transfer of Protected Data, explaining methodology used to filter and eliminate irrelevant Protected Data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Culling activities may include questionnaires, interviews, iterative software searches, deduplication, and compiling data in a jurisdiction not subject to transfer restrictions when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Border Protocol — categorize Protected Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe categories of Protected Data that will be processed or transferred (personal/sensitive personal data, trade secrets, restricted data, consumer data, state secrets, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifying categories helps tailor safeguards and legal analysis under Data Protection Laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Border Protocol — use of protective orders/stipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider using the Model U.S. Federal Court Protective Order or similar protective orders/stipulations with data protection language providing restrictions on use, disclosure, dissemination, and onward transfer; consider redaction and Confidential/Highly Confidential designations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach copies of protective instruments and consider restrictions on onward transfer once Protected Data reaches the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Border Protocol — transparency to data subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive to provide a transparent processing and transfer protocol to Data Subjects, identifying impacted subjects and means to communicate purposes, categories, duties, protections, and other required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications may include postings, one-on-one meetings, group presentations, or notice/acknowledgement documentation requesting consent and Q&A information, in English and local languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Border Protocol — steps to secure transferred data
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify steps taken to secure Protected Data, describing protective measures under the Data Controller, including third-party agreements, protective orders, encryption at rest and in transit, limitations on access, and breach-response procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document encryption technologies, access controls, vendor security, and other technical and contractual safeguards used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Border Protocol — compliance with notification obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe efforts undertaken if notice to regulators, data protection authorities, works councils, or other oversight bodies is contemplated or required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult data protection officers, local counsel, or relevant authorities as appropriate; document the outreach and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Border Protocol — legal basis/mechanism for transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify mechanisms used to legitimize the transfer of Protected Data (e.g., Binding Corporate Rules for intra-group transfers, Privacy Shield certification, Model Contracts, or other transfer safeguards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select mechanisms appropriate to the EU/recipient and transfer purpose; document chosen transfer legal bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Border Protocol — disposition when no longer needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Document procedures used to destroy or return Protected Data to the Data Controller when it is no longer necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include timelines, certification processes, exceptions (legal hold), and methods for secure destruction or return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Border Protocol — designate responsible persons and sign-off
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify those responsible for overseeing preservation, processing, and transfer of Protected Data and obtain their signatures to signify the steps recorded were taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign accountability and include signatures to create a record for regulators evidencing the steps taken to maximize legal compliance.
